findings.message:
Task acceptance not fulfilled: the review found that the candidate does not satisfy source issue #26. Change the candidate so it satisfies everything the issue requires; the reviewer's acceptance evidence:
- public/index.html line 5 keeps width=device-width, initial-scale=1 and drops maximum-scale and user-scalable=no, satisfying that part of the acceptance.
- public/index.html line 99 still registers an unconditional gesturestart handler that calls preventDefault, which suppresses pinch zoom in iOS Safari.
- public/admin_users.html and public/admin_projects.html still declare maximum-scale=1, user-scalable=no at line 5 and include the same gesturestart blocker, so the admin pages still fail the acceptance requirement.
- public/root.html, public/device.html and public/agent_tokens.html also retain the zoom-blocking directives, consistent with the issue statement that the violation applies to every page.

[P1] Pinch zoom remains blocked on iOS by the gesturestart handler

`public/index.html:5` now keeps `width=device-width, initial-scale=1` and removes `maximum-scale`/`user-scalable=no`, but the still-present inline handler at line 99 calls `document.addEventListener('gesturestart', e => e.preventDefault())` unconditionally. iOS Safari ignores `user-scalable=no` and implements pinch zoom through `gesturestart`, so this handler is what actually blocks zooming; until it is removed, pinch zoom will not work on iOS Safari and the acceptance criterion is not met.

public/index.html:5-5

[P2] Admin pages still disable pinch zoom through their viewport meta

Only `public/index.html` was updated, but `public/admin_users.html`, `public/admin_projects.html`, `public/root.html`, `public/device.html` and `public/agent_tokens.html` still declare `maximum-scale=1, user-scalable=no` (and most still include the same `gesturestart` preventDefault). The task states the violation applies to every page and requires pinch zoom to work on the admin pages, so those pages remain non-compliant after this change.
